Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Section 19 meets the preferred position: Services are warranted to be performed professionally and in a workmanlike manner by qualified personnel (19.1), Deliverables conform to documentation and acceptance criteria for ninety days measured from the later of delivery or acceptance and Hosted Services conform throughout the subscription term (19.2), and Vendor warrants no intentionally introduced malicious code and compliance with Applicable Law (19.3). The remedy in 19.4 is re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, escalating to termination and refund of Fees paid, and is expressly non-exclusive for fraud, IP, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims. The disclaimer in 19.5 is mutual and expressly does not limit any express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy, so it does not swallow the express warranty. Section 6 acceptance testing does not shorten the warranty (the 90-day period runs from the later of delivery or acceptance) and Section 3 reinforces the performance standard. No redline needed.

input.quote: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
input.rationale: Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by Customer to Vendor of 15% of annual Fees for each week an invoice is late — a compounding charge triggered by a minor breach (a ten-day payment delay) that within about seven weeks would exceed the entire annual contract value. That is walk-away territory under this rule and fails both the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties) and the fallback (a single early-termination amount capped at three months' fees). No other Customer-payable liquidated damages, minimum-fee or shortfall charges appear: Section 9.4 allows termination without cause with only accrued Fees owed, and Section 27 confirms termination without penalty. We propose deleting the liquidated damages mechanic and substituting simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts as Vendor's sole remedy.

That is walk-away territory under this rule and fails both the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties) and the fallback (a single early-termination amount capped at three months' fees). No other Customer-payable liquidated damages, minimum-fee or shortfall charges appear: Section 9.4 allows termination without cause with only accrued Fees owed, and Section 27 confirms termination without penalty. We propose deleting the liquidated damages mechanic and substituting simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts as Vendor's sole remedy.

proposal.summary: Remove Customer-payable liquidated damages for late payment; replace with simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept liquidated damages payable by us — 15% of annual Fees per week of delay far exceeds any conceivable loss and would quickly outstrip the contract value. Our position is no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties, so we have replaced this with simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Section 22 is the only audit right binding us and it matches the preferred position on every material term: frequency capped at once per twelve months, thirty days' prior written notice, normal business hours with no unreasonable disruption, off-site where practicable, conducted by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds five percent, and an express bar on direct access to Customer systems, unrelated Customer Data, privileged material and third-party confidential information. Section 22.3 adds customer-favourable protections (findings are our Confidential Information, use limited to enforcement, copy of the final report, and payment of a shortfall closing the issue). No verification, inspection, monitoring or remote-access rights appear elsewhere in the document. Nothing to redline.

Original paragraphs:
p0094: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.
p0095: 22.2 Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent for the audited period, in which case Customer will pay reasonable audit costs and the undisputed shortfall. Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information.
p0096: 22.3 Audit findings are Customer Confidential Information and may be used only to enforce this Agreement. Vendor shall provide a copy of the final report. Payment of a shortfall resolves the audited quantity issue absent fraud or demonstrable error.

Resolved definitions:

Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.

Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Customer Data: 1.3 “Customer Data” means all data, records, files, content, personal information, and other materials submitted to, stored in, transmitted through, or otherwise made available to the Services by or for Customer or its Authorized Users, together with output specifically derived from that material. Customer Data excludes anonymized operational telemetry that cannot reasonably be linked to Customer, an Authorized User, or an individual.
Confidential Information: 16.1 “Confidential Information” means non-public information disclosed by or for a Party that is marked confidential or that a reasonable recipient would understand to be confidential given its nature and the circumstances. Customer Data, security information, product plans, pricing, personnel data, and the terms of this Agreement are Confidential Information whether or not marked.

Section 18 (Insurance) already sits at the playbook's **preferred** position on every material term:

| Playbook preferred | Section 18.1 |
|---|---|
| CGL USD 1M/occ, 2M agg | ✅ Matches exactly |
| Professional / E&O USD 2M | ✅ Matches exactly |
| Cyber/privacy USD 5M (data processors) | ✅ Matches exactly |
| Workers' comp as required by law | ✅ Present |
| Certificates on request | ✅ In 18.2 |

The cyber limit is properly calibrated here, since Brightline hosts Customer Data under Sections 15 and 17 — so the USD 5M tier for data-processing vendors is the right trigger, not the fallback USD 2M.

Section 18.2 adds several terms that run in our favour and are better than the model language: reputable insurers, coverage primary to Customer's insurance where customary, advance notice of cancellation or material reduction, and an express statement that insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities (preserving our indemnity and liability rights under Sections 20–21). Coverage also runs for one year post-term, matching the model. Employer's liability of USD 1M is additional cover we did not request.

One minor sub-element noted in the rationale but deliberately not flagged: the cancellation-notice undertaking is qualified by "to the extent available from its insurer" rather than being absolute. Per the classification rules, a missing mechanic of this kind is recorded in the rationale, not raised as a deviation — and pressing it would spend negotiating capital on a clause that otherwise fully meets our ask.

**Finding: deviation (high severity) — Section 7.7 (p0032)**

Section 7.7 requires *Customer* to pay Vendor "as liquidated damages and not as a penalty" 15% of annual Fees **for each week** an invoice is unpaid, triggered by a mere ten-day delay. This compounds to more than the full annual contract value in roughly seven weeks and is triggered by a minor breach — squarely walk-away territory, and failing both the preferred position (no Customer-payable LDs) and the fallback (single early-termination amount capped at three months' fees).

Service credits flowing to us were not flagged.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by Customer to Vendor of 15% of annual Fees for each week an invoice is late — a compounding charge triggered by a minor breach (a ten-day payment delay) that within about seven weeks would exceed the entire annual contract value. That is walk-away territory under this rule and fails both the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties) and the fallback (a single early-termination amount capped at three months' fees). No other Customer-payable liquidated damages, minimum-fee or shortfall charges appear: Section 9.4 allows termination without cause with only accrued Fees owed, and Section 27 confirms termination without penalty. We propose deleting the liquidated damages mechanic and substituting simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts as Vendor's sole remedy.

Original paragraphs:
p0032: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Northwind Analytics, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Brightline Cloud Services Ltd., a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Vendor: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Northwind Analytics, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Brightline Cloud Services Ltd., a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Fees: 1.5 “Fees” means the Implementation Fee.

Rendered redline:
p0032: 7.7 If a proper, undisputed invoice remains unpaid more than thirty days after its due date, Vendor's sole remedy is simple interest on the overdue amount at the lesser of one percent per month or the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law, accruing from the due date until payment. Customer shall not be liable for any liquidated damages, penalty, or similar stipulated amount under this Agreement.

Comment:
[Playbook] We cannot accept liquidated damages payable by us — 15% of annual Fees per week of delay far exceeds any conceivable loss and would quickly outstrip the contract value. Our position is no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties, so we have replaced this with simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts.

Rule:

Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.

Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The Agreement meets the preferred position: Section 2.1 expressly states that no minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies, that Customer pays only for Services ordered under a signed Order Form, and that declining to place further orders is neither a breach nor a shortfall. Section 7.1 bars Vendor from imposing any minimum-use or similar charge not identified in the Order Form, and Section 12.3 confirms Customer has given no exclusivity or minimum-volume commitment. Section 4.1 makes quantity changes a matter of mutually signed change orders, and Section 8.2 lets Customer exit each Order Form on thirty days' notice of non-renewal with no no-downgrade restriction. The only "shortfall" references (Sections 22.2–22.3) are audit true-ups for under-reported usage, not take-or-pay penalties, and payment of a shortfall resolves the issue. You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of Master Services Agreement — verified findings 

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against the playbook. The agreement is, on the whole, unusually favourable to us: indemnification (§ 20), IP and data ownership (§ 14), licence scope (§ 13), assignment and change of control (§ 24), termination for convenience (§ 9.4), renewal mechanics (§ 8), transition assistance and data return (§ 11), warranties (§ 19), audit rights (§ 22), insurance (§ 18) and governing law/venue (§ 28) all meet our preferred positions. The agreement also expressly confirms there is no exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, MFN or minimum-volume obligation binding us (§§ 2.1, 12.3), and the one pricing-parity provision (§ 7.6) runs in our favour.

Two issues require redlines, and both sit in walk-away territory:

1. **Illusory liability cap (§ 21, critical).** The cap is measured by "Fees", which is defined (§§ 1.5/1.6) as the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form. The structure of § 21 is otherwise strong (mutual cap, mutual consequential-damages exclusion, broad Excluded Claims), but the quantum falls far below six months' fees and fails the fallback.
2. **Customer-payable liquidated damages (§ 7.7, high).** A 15% of annual Fees charge per week of late payment compounds past the entire annual contract value in roughly seven weeks, triggered by a minor breach. This fails both the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages) and the fallback (a single early-termination amount capped at three months' fees).

Everything else can be signed as drafted.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 21 Limitation of Liability |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20 Indemnification |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14 Intellectual Property and Deliverables |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes (§ 7.7) |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 Assignment and Change of Control |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13 Access Rights and Licence |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
